THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR DICTATING JUDGMENT,
THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

This appeal is filed under Section-30(1) of the Employees Compensation Act 1923 (hereinafter referred to as 'EC Act' for brevity) by the appellant-insurance company, calling in question the judgment and award dated 27.07.2017, passed in E.C.A. No.73/2014, on the file of the Additional Senior Civil Judge & CJM Tumakuru, (hereinafter referred to as 'the Tribunal' for brevity).

Brief facts:
2. On 29.12.2010, at about 10.00 a.m., at Hemakutta situated near Hampi, Hospet Taluk, the driver of the Bus bearing No.KA-42-8888, instructed the claimant to apply grease to the parts of the Bus.
When the claimant was so engaged in applying grease to the Bus, the driver of the bus without observing the cleaner, suddenly and in negligent manner moved the Bus.
As a result, the wheels of the Bus ran over the left palm of the claimant.

3. Hence, a claim petition was filed by the appellant- claimant under Section-22 of the W.C. Act, claiming compensation for the injuries suffered in the Reliance General Insurance Co Ltd vs Raghu on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82406012/
2 accident during employment.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Tribunal on appreciating the materials on record, allowed the claim petition in part, and awarded a compensation of Rs.2,19,471/-, along with interest at 12% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realisation.
The Tribunal held respondent Nos.1 to 2 therein, jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

4. Heard arguments of the learned counsel for the parties and perused the materials on record.
5.
The learned counsel for the appellant - insurance company submitted that in the present case there is 42 days delay in lodging the complaint before the Police from the date of the alleged accident.

It is further argued that the claimant being Cleaner was under the employment of Respondent No.2 herein had gone in the offending Bus and while he was applying grease to the parts of the bus and at that time, suffered employment injuries and therefore with these allegations the claim petition is filed claiming compensation.

But immediately after the accident, even though the claimant has taken the treatment in the hospital at Hospete, did not inform to the Hospital or to the Police of Hospete city, regarding the accident.
Thereafter the claimant went to Tumkuru and stated to have taken treatment at Tumakuru and thereafter lodged complaint that too after 42 days from the date of the accident.
Therefore, the entire episode is suspicious one.

Hence, without appreciating the evidence on record, the Tribunal wrongly came to the conclusion regarding the alleged accident and awarded the compensation by fastening the liability on the insurance company.

6. Further, submitted that just because there is an existence of insurance policy between the insurance company and the second respondent that cannot be a ground to say that the insurance company is liable to pay the compensation.
Therefore, submitted the entire factum of alleged accident is doubtful one.
Therefore, prays to set-aside the award of the Tribunal.
7. Further, submitted that the second respondent is the owner of the bus who is into the business of bus transportation.
But he did not inform to the insurance company regarding the accident as per clause-(c) of Section-134 of MV Act.

Therefore, this creates doubt regarding the accident and therefore submitted that the insurance company is not liable and if at all the owner admits the accident then the owner may pay the compensation.
Therefore, prays to set-aside the judgment and award of the Tribunal.

8. On the other hand, the learned counsel for respondent No.1 - claimant submitted that the claimant who was working as a cleaner in the bus under the employment of respondent No.2, was running transportation business and the Tribunal has correctly come to the opinion that the claimant had sustained employment injuries and accordingly by considering the insurance policy awarded compensation and fastened the liability on the insurance company.
Therefore, justified that the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.

9. The learned counsel for respondent No.2 - owner submitted that there is no evidence to prove the employer and employee relationship and moreover the Tribunal considering the existence of insurance policy between the appellant and respondent no.2, has fastened the liability on the insurance company.
Therefore, justified the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal and hence prays to dismiss the appeal.

sentences.text: In the present case, the claimant is claiming that he was working as a Cleaner under the employment of the second respondent in bus No.KA-42-8888.
It is the case of the claimant that the second respondent is running bus transport business.

It is the case of the claimant that under the direction of respondent No.2 - owner of the bus, that the claimant went in the bus as a Cleaner to Hemakuta, near Hampi, Hospet Taluk on 29.12.2010 and the claimant had sustained employment injury at morning 10 a.m., but the complaint was lodged on 08.02.2011 after a lapse of 42 days from the date of the accident.

11. It is the case of the claimant that after having sustained injuries in the above said accident, the claimant has taken first aid treatment in the hospital at Hospete and later he returned to Tumakuru and there he has taken treatment in the District Hospital Tumakuru and thereafter lodged a complaint before the Police.
It is stated that on 19.01.2011, a surgery was conducted and on 29.01.2011 the claimant was discharged from the Hospital.
But the fact remains that the accident occurred on 29.12.2010.
By this time 42 days was lapsed for which there is no proper explanation by the claimant.
12. Immediately, after the alleged accident within a reasonable time, there was no intimation either to the Police or to the Insurance Company.
Therefore, this creates suspicion regarding the factum of accident.

Even though there is evidence of the claimant in examination- in-chief that he worked under respondent No.2 - owner - employer, but the employer had not filed any written statement /
objection to the claim petition before the Tribunal.

13. The respondent no.2 - owner had only cross- examined the insurance company official as RW-1 and the cross-examination is only in respect of the particulars of the insurance policy and its existence and not morethan that.
But fundamentally there is a delay of 42 days in lodging the complaint.
There is no evidence on part of the claimant that after the accident, he immediately informed to the owner-employer of the bus regarding the accident.
14. Furthermore, there is no averment made by the employer to have informed the insurance company regarding the alleged accident as per Section-134(c) of MV Act.
Therefore, under these circumstances the appellant - insurance company raised doubt regarding accident, whether the said accident occurred or not, is found to be genuine one.
The second respondent is also silent on the fact whether the accident has occurred or not, whether the claimant had sustained injuries or not.

15. As alleged by the claimant, the second respondent-owner even though appeared before the Tribunal had cross-examined the official of the insurance - 10 - company only, but has not cross-examined the claimant.
Therefore, there is no evidence on record regarding the relationship of employer-employee between second respondent and the claimant respectively.

Reliance General Insurance Co Ltd vs Raghu on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82406012/
4 16.

entities.text: Reliance General Insurance Co Ltd vs Raghu
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The appellant - insurance company's doubt raised regarding the accident and the claimant sustaining injury has found to be proved.
The doubt raised by the insurance company that for claiming compensation from the insurance company, why such scene might not have been created.
Therefore, so far as the insurance company is concerned the doubt raised is found to be expected one.
To indemnify the owner, the proof of accident as alleged and the relationship of the employer-employee is required.
Therefore, there is no prompt action either on part of the claimant or on part of the employer regarding intimating factum of accident to the insurance company.
Therefore, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify the second respondent - employer and to pay the compensation.

Just because the insurance company is held not liable as observed above, that does not foreclose the claimant's case regarding proving the relationship of employer-employees between the claimant and the second respondent.
Even though the claimant has stated in the examination-in-chief that he was working as a cleaner in the bus, but there is no evidence that he had informed the employer soon after the accident.
Also there is no evidence that the second respondent - employer had intimated this accident to the insurance company as required under Section-134(c) of MV Act.

Therefore, on this question the adjudication of dispute between the claimant and the second respondent - employer in order to prove the relationship of the employer-employee and regarding occurrence of the accident, whether there was any information to the employer, the case is liable to be remanded to the Tribunal.

. But so far as the appellant-insurance company is concerned for want of proof regarding the alleged accident and having sustained injuries in the said accident, the doubt raised by the insurance company is found to be feasible.

Therefore, the matter is remanded to the Tribunal so far as the dispute between the employer and claimant regarding compensation to be determined and to give evidence in this regard regarding relationship of the employer-employee, therefore to this question only the matter is remanded to the Tribunal for reconsideration on this aspect.
Therefore, the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is liable to be set-aside.

Hence, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i.
The appeal is Allowed.

ii. The impugned judgment and award dated 27.07.2017, passed in E.C.A.
No.73/2014, passed by the Additional Senior Civil Judge & CJM Tumakuru is hereby set-aside.
The matter is remanded to the Tribunal, so far as the dispute regarding the claimant and second respondent-employer regarding relationship of employer-employee.

Reliance General Insurance Co Ltd vs Raghu on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82406012/
5 iv.

sentences.text: The parties shall appear before the Tribunal on 31.05.2023, without expecting any further notice in this regard.
The Tribunal shall consider the matter afresh in accordance with law and shall dispose of the matter within six months thereafter.
v. The parties are at liberty to adduce further evidence and file additional material if they are so advised.
vi. The amount in deposit by the Insurance company shall be refunded to the Appellant- Insurance company through Digital Payment.
vii. Registry is directed to return the Trial Court Records to the Tribunal, along with certified - 14 - copy of the order passed by this Court forthwith without any delay.

viii. Draw award accordingly.
ix.
No order as to costs.
